extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, recipients, and grants management officials (GMO/IC staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and standards for NIH grant payments, cash management, allowable costs, indirect cost treatment, cost transfers, and related post-award financial administration that applicants and recipients must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual progress report for non-competing continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to submit an annual progress report as a prerequisite to NIH approval and funding of each subsequent budget period (non-competing continuation award) within an approved project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision to fund the next budget period will be formalized by issuance of the Notice of Award (NoA) indicating new budget period and amount. NIH may withhold support for reasons in enforcement actions; recipients may appeal withholding only if it was for failure to comply with prior award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting to close fixed year appropriation accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must report disbursements on the Federal Financial Report (FFR) no later than August 31 of the fifth fiscal year after the year of availability to allow agencies to close appropriation accounts by September 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet this deadline may limit carryover availability and may limit or eliminate authority to extend the final budget period for multiyear-funded awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Award (NoA) budget adherence and rebudgeting flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each NoA sets forth the amount of funds awarded, shown either as categorical budget or total direct costs plus indirect costs; recipients have certain rebudgeting flexibility within the overall amount awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More significant post-award changes require NIH prior approval (see Changes in Project and Budget). The recipient may be required to provide matching funds under construction awards if specified in the NoA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of additional/special terms for inadequate management systems
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may use additional or more restrictive terms and conditions if the GMO finds the recipient’s management systems and practices are not adequate to ensure appropriate stewardship of NIH funds or to achieve award objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include requiring prior approval for expenditures that ordinarily do not require it, providing more frequent reports, closer monitoring, or assistance to take corrective action. Authorities include 42 CFR Part 52.9, 2 CFR Part 200.339, and 45 CFR Part 75.371.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance payment drawdown timing (cash management standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although grants may be financed by advance payments, recipients are expected to draw funds on an as‑needed basis—specifically, no more than 3 business days before funds are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds deposited as an unrestricted advance should be fully disbursed (checks written, signed, and issued) by the close of business the next workday after receipt. Recipients are responsible for determining deposit timing, ensuring disbursement, and immediately returning undisbursed Federal funds to PMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance standards for consortium participants and contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Advances made by recipients to consortium participants and contractors under grants must conform to substantially the same standards of timing and amount that govern advances to the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass-through of advance payments should not create longer or larger cash-on-hand than permitted for the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment requests require detailed justification (DTS review)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH grant recipients are required to include a detailed justification explaining why funds are being drawn and how funds are being used when submitting payment requests to PMS to allow NIH staff timely review under the Defend the Spend (DTS) system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of Executive Order 14222 implementation to enhance transparency and reduce waste, fraud, and abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMARTLINK II/ACH eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: SMARTLINK II/ACH advance payment method makes direct deposit and requires Internet access to submit a request; provides funds the day following the request via ACH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must be eligible for unrestricted advance via SMARTLINK II/ACH to use this expedited method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash request submission timing and conversion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients not eligible for unrestricted advance via SMARTLINK must submit a cash request, usually monthly, which may be advance or reimbursement as specified by the awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For timely receipt, submit requests early enough to be forwarded to PMS at least 2 weeks before cash is needed. Recipients may be converted from unrestricted advance to cash request basis if financial management systems do not meet standards or if not complying with cash management/reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest on advances and interest-bearing accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients subject to 2 CFR Part 200 who receive advance payments must maintain those advances in an interest-bearing account and must remit interest earned annually to HHS PMS, except amounts up to $500 per year may be retained for administrative expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are expected to promptly return any funds not spent within three business days. Interest/fees resulting from underpayments paid correctly are not considered improper payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper payments prevention and documentation (IPERIA/Do Not Pay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper payments occur when funds go to wrong recipient, incorrect amounts, lack documentation, or improper use; agencies should ensure documentation requirements are necessary and avoid imposing burdensome requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS integrates the Do Not Pay system into PMS processes to reduce improper payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget compliance with cost principles
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant’s budget request is reviewed for compliance with governing cost principles and other requirements/policies applicable to recipient and award type; resulting award includes a budget consistent with these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH anticipates post-award budget modifications may be needed; significant deviations require NIH prior approval. The GMO monitors expenditures for conformance with cost policies and may use audit findings for final cost adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allowability four tests (Reasonableness, Allocability, Consistency, Conformance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost principles address four tests to determine allowability: Reasonableness, Allocability, Consistency, and Conformance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tests apply regardless of direct/indirect treatment or whether category specified in cost principles. The fact that a proposed cost was awarded does not indicate allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness (cost test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost may be considered reasonable if it does not exceed an amount that a prudent person would incur under the circumstances prevailing when the decision to incur the cost was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether cost is generally necessary for operations or grant performance, whether recipient complied with its policies, and whether responsible individuals acted with due prudence toward the Federal government, public, and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocability (cost test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost is allocable to a specific grant, function, or cost objective if assignable in accordance with relative benefits received or other equitable relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cost is allocable as a direct cost if incurred solely to advance work under the grant or meets closely related projects determination. Costs benefiting multiple projects should be allocated proportionally where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency (cost test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must be consistent in assigning costs to cost objectives; costs may be charged as either direct or indirect as appropriate, but must be treated consistently for all work of the organization under similar circumstances regardless of funding source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inconsistent charging or double charging of costs between direct and indirect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance (cost test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs must conform with limitations and exclusions in the terms and conditions of award, including those in the cost principles; conformance varies by activity type, recipient type, and award characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Cost Considerations—Allowability of Costs/Activities and IIB for distinctions by grant/recipient type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct vs. indirect cost identification and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs can be identified specifically with a sponsored project or institutional activity (e.g., salaries, travel, equipment, supplies); indirect costs (F&A) are for common/joint objectives not readily identified to an individual project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must manage and account costs consistently and must not include costs associated with the indirect cost rate as direct costs. Project costs = allowable direct costs + allocable portion of allowable indirect costs - applicable credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost rate negotiation and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect cost rates are negotiated with cognizant agencies (e.g., CAS, DFAS for for-profits) and must be prepared per applicable cost principles and guidance; applicability depends on recipient type and award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advised to establish a rate, GMO will indicate responsible office. NIH generally will not provide indirect costs without an established rate except where policy provides fixed rates or other exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis indirect cost rate option (10% MTDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients/subrecipients without a current Federal negotiated indirect cost rate may elect to charge a de minimis rate of 10% of modified total direct costs (MTDC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies/pass-through entities may not require a de minimis lower than negotiated or elected rate unless required by statute. Costs must be consistently charged as direct or indirect and may not be double charged. De minimis may be used indefinitely until the recipient chooses to seek a negotiated rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-through entity responsibilities for subrecipient indirect rates
rubrics_metrics.description: If a subrecipient already has a negotiated indirect cost rate with their cognizant agency, the pass-through entity must accept it; if no approved rate exists, the pass-through entity must determine rate in collaboration with the subrecipient (prior negotiated rate or de minimis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTE must not require de minimis if subrecipient has Federally approved rate; PTE may, but is not required to, negotiate a rate with a proposed subrecipient who requests it. For for-profit consortium members, an established indirect cost rate is required before charging indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of awards not reimbursed for indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH does not reimburse indirect costs under specific classes of awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed classes include: Fellowships (e.g., Kirschstein-NRSA individual fellowships), Construction and Modernization grants, Grants to Individuals, Grants to Federal Institutions, Grants in Support of Scientific Meetings (Conference Grants), and Endowment Grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special treatment of high-volume Genomic Arrays (GA) purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: High-volume purchases of genomic arrays (GA) in excess of $50,000 per year will not be treated as 'supplies' for indirect base purposes; instead GA over $50,000 will be treated using the subcontract (consortium/contractual cost) surrogate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each budget year, first $50,000 of GA treated as supplies; GA in excess of $50,000 use subcontract surrogate to provide consistent budgeting, accounting and reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed indirect cost provisions for certain award classes and foreign organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH provides indirect costs without negotiated rate under certain classes at fixed rates: e.g., Kirschstein-NRSA institutional research training and K awards at 8% of MTDC (exclusions apply); grants to foreign organizations generally funded at 8% MTDC with exceptions (e.g., AUB, WHO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 8% excludes tuition and related fees, equipment, and subawards in excess of $25,000. Foreign organizations are not supported for capital expenses/facilities; some items normally treated as indirect costs may be requested as direct costs and evaluated for allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost transfer correction timing and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost transfers that represent corrections of clerical or bookkeeping errors should be accomplished within 90 days of when the error was discovered and must be supported by documentation that fully explains how the error occurred and a certification of correctness by a responsible official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explanation like 'to correct error' is not sufficient. Transfers solely to cover cost overruns are not allowable. Recipients must maintain documentation per 2 CFR 200.337 and make it available for audit or review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls, detection of errors, and corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should have systems to detect errors within a reasonable time frame; untimely discovery or frequent errors may indicate poor internal controls requiring improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may require corrective action or impose additional award terms and conditions if deficiencies are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring of expenditure patterns and GMO actions for accelerated/delayed expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: The GMO monitors recipient expenditure rates within budget and project periods; accelerated or delayed expenditures may indicate deficient financial management or internal controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expenditure patterns raise concern, GMO may request additional information, restrict expenditures, or make adjustments. Accelerated/delayed expenditures could threaten completion within approved budget/period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of shared costs and closely related work rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When costs (e.g., salaries) support two or more sources, costs that benefit multiple projects in determinable proportions should be allocated based on proportional benefit; if proportions cannot be determined due to interrelationship, costs may be allocated on any reasonable basis provided they are allowable, allocable, reasonable, and the accounting system includes adequate internal controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate internal controls include appropriate segregation of duties (e.g., no one person has complete control over a financial transaction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable credits treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable credits (transactions that offset or reduce direct or indirect cost items such as purchase discounts, rebates, recoveries) must be treated as an adjustment on the recipient’s FFR whether those credits accrue during or after the period of grant support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIH awarding IC will notify recipients of any additional actions needed; see cost principles for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of services provided by affiliated organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for services provided by affiliated but legally independent organizations (e.g., foundations) must be appropriately accounted for when included in an organization's indirect proposal or charged to NIH awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful treatment is required to avoid inappropriate inclusion of parent organization services or double counting in indirect proposals; documentation and consistency with cost principles are expected.
